012.title: Introduction to Media Computation
012.description: Introduction to key computational ideas necessary to understand and produce digital media. Fundamentals of programming and analysis of how media are represented and transmitted in digital form. Aimed primarily at non-computer science students.
012.credit_limit_text: Only 2 units of credit for students that have taken ECS 010, ECS 030, ECS 032A, ECS 032AV, ECS 036A or ENG 006.

017.title: Data, Logic, & Computing
017.description: Display, processing, and representation of information and data on a computer. Understanding and analyzing the digital representations of numbers, images, and sounds. Basic computer operations and their logic. Introduction to discrete mathematics in computer science, including propositional logic, proofs by induction, recursions, and counting. Introduction to algorithms. Uses of computers and their influence on society.
017.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed course ECS 020 or MAT108.
017.prereq_text: MAT 016A (can be concurrent) or MAT 017A (can be concurrent) or MAT 019A { can be concurrent } or MAT 021A (can be concurrent).

020.title: Discrete Mathematics For Computer Science
020.description: Discrete mathematics of particular utility to computer science. Proofs by induction. Propositional and first-order logic. Sets, functions, and relations. Big-O and related notations. Recursion and solutions of recurrence relations. Combinatorics. Probability on finite probability spaces. Graph theory.
020.prereq_text: MAT 016A C- or better or MAT 017A C- or better or MAT 019A C- or better or MAT 021A C- or better.

032AV.title: Introduction to Programming
032AV.description: Introduction to programming and problem solving in Python. Aimed primarily at non-major students.
032AV.credit_limit_text: No credit to students who have completed ECS 032B, ECS 032C, ECS 036A, ECS 036B, ECS 036C.

032B.title: Introduction to Data Structures
032B.description: Design and analysis of data structures using Python; trees, heaps, searching, sorting, and graphs.
032B.credit_limit_text: No credit to students who have completed ECS 036B, ECS 036C, ECS 040 or ECS 060.
032B.prereq_text: ECS 032A C- or better or ECS 032AV C- or better or ECS 036A C- or better.

034.title: Software Development in UNIX & C++
034.description: UNIX Operating system tools and programming environment. Methods for debugging and verification. Principles object-oriented programming in C++.
034.credit_limit_text: No credit to students who have completed ECS 036B, ECS 036C, ECS 040 or ECS 060.
034.prereq_text: ECS 032C C- or better; or consent of instructor.

036A.title: Programming & Problem Solving
036A.description: Programming in modern C++ for students with prior experience. Fundamental programming constructs, abstraction using functions and basic classes, algorithmic design, and debugging. Emphasis on good programming style and effective use of UNIX-based development tools.
036A.credit_limit_text: Only 2 units of credit to students who have completed ECS 032A or ECS 032AV; no credit to students who have completed ECS 032B, ECS 032C, ECS 034, ECS 040 or ECS 060.
036A.prereq_text: ECS 032A C- or better or ECS 032AV C- or better; or must satisfy computer science placement exam; prior experience with basic programming concepts (variable, loops, conditional statements) required.

036B.title: Software Development & Object-Oriented Programming
036B.description: Advanced software development and object-oriented programming in modern C++. Implementation of substantial programs. Emphasis on software engineering practices, automation, and debugging.
036B.credit_limit_text: No credit to students who have completed ECS 032B, ECS 032C, ECS 034, ECS 040, or ECS 060.

092.title: Internship in Computer Science
092.description: Supervised work experience in computer science.
092.prereq_text: Lower division standing; project approval prior to period of internship.

099.title: Special Study for Lower Division Students
099.description: Special study for lower division students.

111.title: Applied Machine Learning for Non-Majors
111.description: Machine learning methods and their application. Theory, design and evaluation of supervised/unsupervised machine learning algorithms. Practical use of matching learning methods and their challenges.
111.credit_limit_text: No credit if student has taken ECS 171; not intended for Computer Science and Computer Science Engineering Majors.
111.prereq_text: (ECS 032B or ECS 036C); (MAT 022A or MAT 027A or MAT 067); (MAT 135A or STA 035B or STA 131A or MAT 107).

117.title: Algorithms for Data Science
117.description: Algorithms for searching, pattern matching, combinatorial problems, clustering, and time series analysis with practical emphasis.
117.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit for students who have completed ECS 122A
117.prereq_text: ECS 017 or ECS 020; ECS 032B or ECS 036C.

120.title: Theory of Computation
120.description: Fundamental ideas in the theory of computation, including formal languages, computability and complexity. Reducibility among computational problems.

122A.title: Algorithm Design & Analysis
122A.description: Complexity of algorithms, bounds on complexity, analysis methods. Searching, sorting, pattern matching, graph algorithms. Algorithm design techniques: divide-conquer, greedy, dynamic programming. Approximation methods. NP-complete problems.

122B.title: Algorithm Design & Analysis
122B.description: Theory and practice of hard problems, and problems with complex algorithm solutions. NP-completeness, approximation algorithms, randomized algorithms, dynamic programming and branch and bound. Theoretical analysis, implementation and practical evaluations. Examples from parallel, string, graph, and geometric algorithms.

124.title: Theory & Practice of Bioinformatics
124.description: Fundamental biological, mathematical and algorithmic models underlying bioinformatics and systems biology; sequence analysis, database search, genome annotation, clustering and classification, functional gene networks, regulatory network inference, phylogenetic trees, applications of common bioinformatics tools in molecular biology and genetics.
124.prereq_text: (ECS 032A or ECS 032AV or ECS 036A or ENG 006); (STA 032 or STA 035B or STA 100 or STA 131A or ECS 132 or MAT 135A or EEC 161 or BIM 105); (BIS 002A or MCB 010).

132.title: Probability & Statistical Modeling for Computer Science
132.description: Univariate and multivariate distributions. Estimation and model building. Markov/Hidden Markov models. Applications to data mining, networks, security, software engineering and bioinformatics.
132.prereq_text: (ECS 040 or ECS 034 or ECS 036B); ECS 020; MAT 021C; (MAT 022A or MAT 027A or MAT 067).

140A.title: Programming Languages
140A.description: Syntactic definition of programming languages. Introduction to programming language features including variables, data types, data abstraction, object-orientedness, scoping, parameter disciplines, exception handling. Non-imperative programming languages. Comparative study of several high-level programming languages.

150.title: Operating Systems & System Programming
150.description: Basic concepts of operating systems and system programming. Processes and interprocess communication/synchronization; virtual memory, program loading and linking; file and I/O subsystems; utility programs. Study of a real operating system.
150.prereq_text: (ECS 034 or ECS 036C or ECS 060); (ECS 154A or EEC 170).

152A.title: Computer Networks
152A.description: Overview of computer networks, TCP/IP protocol suite, computer-networking applications and protocols, transport-layer protocols, network architectures, Internet Protocol (IP), routing, link-layer protocols, local area and wireless networks, medium access control, physical aspects of data transmission, and network-performance analysis.
152A.credit_limit_text: Only 2 units of credit for students who have taken ECS 157.
152A.prereq_text: (ECS 032B or ECS 036C); (ECS 132 or EEC 161 or MAT 135A or STA 032 or STA 035B or STA 100 or STA 131A).

154A.title: Computer Architecture
154A.description: Introduction to digital design. Interfacing of devices for I/O, memory and memory management. Input/output programming, via wait loops, hardware interrupts and calls to operating system services. Hardware support for operating systems software.
154A.credit_limit_text: Only 1 unit of credit allowed for students who have taken EEC 170.

154B.title: Computer Architecture
154B.description: Hardwired and microprogrammed CPU design. Memory hierarchies. Uniprocessor performance analysis under varying program mixes. Introduction to pipelining and multiprocessors.
154B.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken ECS 201A.

160.title: Software Engineering
160.description: Requirements, specification, design, implementation, testing, and verification of large software systems. Study and use of software engineering methodologies.

162.title: Web Programming
162.description: Technical aspects of building websites, including both server-side and client-side software development.
162.prereq_text: ECS 030 or ECS 034 or ECS 036B; or equivalent programming experience in C and the Unix environment.

164.title: Human-Computer Interaction
164.description: Introduction to concepts and practice of modern human-computer interaction design.

170.title: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence
170.description: Design and implementation of intelligent computer systems. Knowledge representation and organization. Memory and inference. Problem solving. Natural language processing.

171.title: Machine Learning
171.description: Introduction to machine learning. Supervised & unsupervised learning, including classification, dimensionality reduction, regression & clustering using modern machine learning methods. Applications of machine learning to other fields.
171.prereq_text: (ECS 032B or ECS 036C); (STA 032 or STA 035B or STA 100 or STA 131A or MAT 135A or EEC 161 or ECS 132); (MAT 022A or MAT 027A or MAT 067).

175.title: Computer Graphics
175.description: Principles of computer graphics, with a focus on interactive systems. Current graphics hardware, elementary operations in two-and three-dimensional space, geometric transformations, camera models and interaction, graphics system design, standard graphics APIs, individual projects.
175.prereq_text: (ECS 060 or ECS 034 or ECS 036C); (MAT 022A or MAT 027A or MAT 067).

189G.title: Special Topics in Computer Science: Artificial Intelligence

193A.title: Capstone Project
193A.description: Responding to real-life client design challenges, student teams plan, implement, and evaluate large-scale projects involving computer and computational systems. Project supervised by a faculty member. Must take ECS 193A & ECS 193B to receive credit.
193A.prereq_text: ECS 160 (can be concurrent); ECS 150; upper division standing in Computer Science or Computer Science & Engineering; or consent of instructor.

198F.title: Student Facilitated Course
198F.description: Student facilitated course intended primarily for upper division students.

201A.title: Advanced Computer Architecture
201A.description: Modern research topics and methods in computer architecture. Design implications of memory latency and bandwidth limitations. Performance enhancement via within-processor and between-processor parallelism.
201A.credit_limit_text: One unit of credit if student has previously taken ECS 154B after Fall 2019.

232.title: Theory of Molecular Computation
232.description: Theory of chemical reaction networks, molecular circuits, DNA self-assembly, DNA sequence design and thermodynamic energy models, and connections to the field of distributed computing.
232.prereq_text: ECS 120 or ECS 220 recommended; probability course recommended, for example ECS 132 or MAT 135A or STA 012 or STA 131A or MAT 131A; or consent of instructor.

251.title: Operating Systems
251.description: Models, design, implementation, performance evaluation in operating systems. Algorithms, internal architectures for single processor OS and distributed systems. Concurrency control, recovery, security. OS kernel-level programming. Special topics embedded systems, real-time system, device driver, NPU (Network Processor Unit).

260.title: Software Engineering
260.description: Advanced techniques for domain-specific software reuse.

261.title: Program Verification
261.description: Methods of proving correctness of programs with respect to formal specifications, with attention to those suited for employing automated deduction. Logic background, symbolic execution, techniques suited to iterative programming, methods from denotational semantics, termination, dynamic logic and proofs of concurrent programs.
261.prereq_text: PHI 112; or MAT 125 or familiarity with first-order logic; knowledge of an integrative and functional programming language.

272.title: Information Visualization
272.description: Advanced topics in information visualization: perceptually effective display methods, color design and selection, interaction models and techniques, focus-context techniques, distortion methods, large graph visualization techniques, visual data mining methods, and evaluation methods.

289G.title: Special Topics in Computer Science: Artificial Intelligence

007.title: Introduction to Programming & Microcontrollers
007.description: Programming computers using C/C++ languages. Software engineering and object-oriented design. Programming for hardware devices.
007.credit_limit_text: Only 2 units of credit for students who have previously taken ECS 036A or ECS 032A or ECS 032AV..

018.title: Digital Systems I
018.description: Introduction to digital system design including combinational logic design, sequential and asynchronous circuits, computer arithmetic, memory systems and algorithmic state machine design; computer aided design (CAD) methodologies and tools.
018.credit_limit_text: No credit to students who have previously completed EEC 180A.

100.title: Circuits II
100.description: Theory, application, and design of analog circuits. Methods of analysis including frequency response, SPICE simulation, and Laplace transform. Operational amplifiers and design of active filters.
100.credit_limit_text: Students who have completed ENG 100 may receive 3.5 units of credit.
100.prereq_text: (ENG 017 C- or better or ENG 017V C- or better); (MAT 022B or MAT 027B); EEC 010; or consent of instructor.

110A.title: Electronic Circuits I
110A.description: Use and modeling of nonlinear solid-state electronic devices in basic analog and digital circuits. Introduction to the design of transistor amplifiers and logic gates.
110A.prereq_text: EEC 100; (EEC 140A (can be concurrent) or EEC 140AV (can be concurrent) or EEC 111 (can be concurrent)).

112.title: Communication Electronics
112.description: Electronic circuits for analog and digital communication, including oscillators, mixers, tuned amplifiers, modulators, demodulators, and phase-locked loops. Circuits for amplitude modulation (AM) and frequency modulation (FM) are emphasized.

130B.title: Introductory Electromagnetics II
130B.description: Plane wave propagation in lossy media, reflections, guided waves, simple modulated waves and dispersion, and basic antennas.

134A.title: RF/Microwave Systems Design
134A.description: Board-level RF design, fabrication, and characterization of an RF/microwave system, including the antenna, RF front-end, baseband, mix-signal circuits, and digital signal processing models.

136A.title: Electronic Design Project
136A.description: Optical, electronic and communication-engineering design of an opto-electronic system operating under performance and economic constraints. Measurement techniques will be designed and implemented, and the system will be characterized.
136A.prereq_text: (ECS 036B or EEC 007); EEC 018; EEC 100; (EEC 110B or EEC 180 or EEC 157A (can be concurrent) or EEC 157AV (can be concurrent)).

146A.title: Integrated Circuits Fabrication
146A.description: Theoretical and experimental study of basic fabrication processes for metal oxide semiconductor integrated circuits, including oxidation, photolithography, impurity diffusion, metallization, wet chemical etching, and characterization.

150.title: Introduction to Signals & Systems
150.description: Characterization and analysis of continuous-time linear systems. Fourier series and transforms with applications. Introduction to communication systems. Transfer functions and block diagrams. Elements of feedback systems. Stability of linear systems.

157AV.title: Control Systems
157AV.description: Analysis and design of feedback control systems. Examples drawn from electrical and mechanical systems as well as other engineering fields. Mathematical modeling of systems, stability criteria, root-locus and frequency domain design methods.

161.title: Applied Probability for Electrical & Computer Engineers
161.description: Axioms of probability, discrete and continuous random variables, expectation and moments. Transformation of random variables. Joint and conditional densities. Limit theorems, Markov and Poisson processes. Applications in Electrical and Computer Engineering.

172.title: Embedded Systems
172.description: Introduction to embedded-system hardware and software. Topics include: embedded processor and memory architecture; input/output hardware and software, including interrupts and direct memory access; interfacing with sensors and actuators; wired and wireless embedded networking.

173A.title: Computer Networks
173A.description: Overview of computer networks, TCP/IP protocol suite, computer-networking applications and protocols, transport-layer protocols, network architectures, Internet Protocol (IP), routing, link-layer protocols, local area and wireless networks, medium access control, physical aspects of data transmission, and network-performance analysis.
173A.credit_limit_text: Only 2 units of credit for students who have taken ECS 157.
173A.prereq_text: (ECS 032B or ECS 036C); (ECS 132 or EEC 161 or MAT 135A or STA 131A or STA 100 or STA 032, STA 035B).

180.title: Digital Systems II
180.description: Computer-aided design of digital systems with emphasis on hardware description languages (VHDL), logic synthesis, and field-programmable gate arrays (FPGA). May cover advanced topics in digital system design such as static timing analysis, pipelining, memory system design, testing digital circuits.
180.credit_limit_text: No credit to students who have previously completed EEC 180B.

193A.title: Senior Design Project
193A.description: Team design project for seniors in Electrical or Computer Engineering. Project involves analysis, design, implementation and evaluation of an Electrical Engineering or Computer Engineering system. Project is supervised by a faculty member.
193A.prereq_text: EEC 196 (can be concurrent); and consent of instructor.

195A.title: Autonomous Vehicle Design Project
195A.description: Design and construct an autonomous race car. Work in groups to design, build and test speed control circuits, track sensing circuits, and a steering control loop.
195A.prereq_text: (ECS 036A or EEC 007); EEC 018; (EEC 110B or EEC 157A (can be concurrent) or EEC 157AV (can be concurrent) or ECS 036B).

201.title: Digital Signal Processing
201.description: Theory and design of digital filters. Classification of digital filters, linear phase systems, all-pass functions, FIR and IIR filter design methods and optimality measures, numerically robust structures for digital filters.
201.prereq_text: EEC 150B; STA 120 or MAT 131 or MAT 167 recommended.

212.title: Analog MOS IC Design for Signal Processing
212.description: Analysis and design of analog MOS integrated circuits. Passive components, Single-ended and fully differential op amps, Sampled-data and continuous-time filters.

230.title: Electromagnetics
230.description: Maxwell's equations, plane waves, reflection and refraction, complex waves, waveguides, resonant cavities, and basic antennas.

235.title: Photonics
235.description: Optical propagation of electromagnetic waves and beams in photonic components and the design of such devices using numerical techniques.

243.title: Optical Imaging & Microscopy
243.description: Theory and techniques of optical imaging & microscopy. Fourier optics; light propagation & light detection; imaging contrast mechanisms; optical & microscopy techniques.

244.title: Introduction to Neuroengineering
244.description: Survey of neuroengineering field from engineering and biological perspectives; micro-/nano-fabrication technology; optical and electrical techniques to monitor and modulate neural activity; computational tools and control systems; prosthetics and human machine interfaces; human performance and rehabilitation; cognitive neuroengineering; neuroethics; extensive proposal development to merge aforementioned themes into a multidisciplinary project.
244.prereq_text: Graduate standing; or consent of instructor.

264.title: Estimation & Detection of Signals in Noise
264.description: Introduction to parameter estimation and detections of signals in noise. Bayes and Neyman-Pearson likelihood-ratio tests for signal detection. Maximum-likelihood parameter estimation. Detection of known and Gaussian signals in white or colored noise.  Applications to communications, radar, signal processing.

270.title: Computer Architecture
270.description: Introduction to modern techniques for high-performance single and multiple processor systems. Topics include advanced pipeline design, advanced memory hierarchy design, optimizing pipeline and memory use, and memory sharing among multiprocessors. Case studies of recent single and multiple processor systems.

273.title: Networking Architecture & Resource Management
273.description: Design & implementation principles of networking architecture and protocols. Internet, data center, and telephony case studies. Topics: Internet data & control planes; application & services; resource management; Quality of Service (QoS) provisioning; traffic engineering; performance evaluation, software-defined networks, & future research issues.

281.title: VLSI Digital Signal Processing
281.description: Digital signal processors, building blocks, and algorithms. Design and implementation of processor algorithms, architectures, control, functional units, and circuit topologies for increased performance and reduced circuit size and power dissipation.
281.prereq_text: EEC 150B; EEC 170; (EEC 180 or EEC 180B); or consent of instructor.

283.title: Advanced Design Verification of Digital Systems
283.description: Design verification techniques for digital systems; simulation-based design verification techniques; formal verification techniques, including equivalence checking, model checking, and theorem proving; timing analysis and verification; application of design certification techniques to microprocessors.

289A.title: Special Topics in Electrical & Computer Engineering: Computer Science

289K.title: Special Topics in Electrical & Computer Engineering: High Frequency Phenomena & Devices
289K.description: Special topics in High Frequency Phenomena & Devices.

289O.title: Special Topics in Electrical & Computer Engineering: Integrated Circuits

290.title: Seminar in Electrical & Computer Engineering
290.description: Discussion and presentation of current research and development in Electrical & Computer Engineering.

001A.title: Principles of Microeconomics
001A.description: ECN 001A & ECN 001B may be taken in either order. Analysis of the allocation of resources and the distribution of income through a price system; competition and monopoly; the role of public policy; comparative economic systems.

001AV.title: Principles of Microeconomics
001AV.description: Analysis of the allocation of resources and the distribution of income through a price system; competition and monopoly; the role of public policy; comparative economic systems.
001AV.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken ECN 001A.

001B.title: Principles of Macroeconomics
001B.description: ECN 001A & ECN 001B may be taken in either order. Analysis of the economy as a whole; determinants of the level of income, employment and prices; money and banking, economic fluctuations, international trade, economic development; the role of public policy.

092.title: Internship & Field Work
092.description: Intensive study of practical application of concepts in economics, stressing research methods and empirical analysis.

100A.title: Intermediate Micro Theory: Consumer & Producer Theory
100A.description: Consumer and producer theory. Equilibrium and welfare analysis. Topics include competitive markets, consumer and producer surplus at an intermediate level.
100A.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students that have taken ARE 100A
100A.prereq_text: (ECN 001A C- or better or ECN 001AV C- or better or ECN 001AY C- or better); (ECN 001B C- or better or ECN 001BV C- or better); ((MAT 016A C- or better, MAT 016B C- or better, MAT 016C C- or better) or (MAT 017A C- or better, MAT 017B C- or better) or (MAT 019A C- or better, MAT 019B C- or better, MAT 019C C- or better) or (MAT 021A C- or better, MAT 021B C- or better)).

100B.title: Intermediate Micro Theory: Imperfect Competition & Market Failure
100B.description: Imperfect competition and market failure. Topics include exchange, monopoly, game theory, uncertainty, asymmetric information, and public goods.
100B.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students that have taken ARE 100B.

101.title: Intermediate Macro Theory
101.description: Theory of income, employment and prices under static and dynamic conditions, and long term growth.
101.prereq_text: (ECN 001A C- or better or ECN 001AY C- or better or ECN 001AV C- or better); (ECN 001B C- or better or ECN 001BV C- or better); ((MAT 016A C- or better, MAT 016B C- or better, MAT 016C C- or better) or (MAT 017A C- or better, MAT 017B C- or better) or (MAT 019A C- or better, MAT 019B C- or better, MAT 019C C- or better) or (MAT 021A C- or better, MAT 021B C- or better)).

102.title: Analysis of Economic Data
102.description: Analysis of economic data to investigate key relationships emphasized in introductory micro and macro economics. Obtaining, transforming, displaying data; statistical analysis of economic data; basic univariate and multivariate regression analysis.
102.prereq_text: (ECN 001A or ECN 001AY or ECN 001AV); (ECN 001B or ECN 001BV); (STA 013 or STA 013V or STA 013Y or STA 032); ((MAT 016A, MAT 016B, MAT 016C) or (MAT 017A, MAT 017B) or (MAT 019A, MAT 019B, MAT 019C) or (MAT 021A or MAT 021B)); or consent of instructor.

111B.title: Economics History
111B.description: Survey of economic change in the United States from 1865 to the post World War II era.
111B.prereq_text: (ECN 001A or ECN 001AY or ECN 001AV); (ECN 001B or ECN 001BV); or consent of instructor.

115A.title: Economic Development
115A.description:
Major issues encountered in emerging from international poverty, including problems of growth and structural change, human welfare,
population growth and health, labor markets and internal migration. Important issues of policy concerning international trade and industrialization.
115A.prereq_text: (ECN 001A or ECN 001AY or ECN 001AV); (ECN 001B or ECN 001BV).

117.title: Economics of International Immigration
117.description: Introduction to research on the economics of immigration. Immigrant demographics and reasons for migrating. Immigrant success and effects on native populations. Influence of immigrants on those left behind. Discussion of migration policy in the US and other countries.
117.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have previously completed an upper division economics course in international immigration.
117.prereq_text: (ECN 001A or ECN 001AY or ECN 001AV); (ECN 001B or ECN 001BV).

122.title: Theory of Games & Strategic Behavior
122.description: Introduction to game theory. Explanation of the behavior of rational individuals with interacting and often conflicting interests. Non-cooperative and cooperative theory. Applications to economics, political science and other fields.
122.prereq_text: (MAT 016A C- or better, MAT 016B C- or better, MAT 016C C- or better) or (MAT 017A C- or better, MAT 017B C- or better) or (MAT 019A C- or better, MAT 019B C- or better, MAT 019C C- or better) or (MAT 021A C- or better, MAT 021B C- or better); or consent of instructor.

134.title: Financial Economics
134.description: General background and rationale of corporation; finance as resource allocation over time; decision making under uncertainty and the role of information; capital market and interest rate structure; financial decisions.
134.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed ARE 171.
134.prereq_text: (ECN 100A or ECN 100AV or ECN 100AY or ARE 100A); (STA 013 or STA 013V or STA 013Y); (ECN 100B or ARE 100B).

135.title: Money, Banks, & Financial Institutions
135.description: Banks and the banking system. Uncertainty and asymmetric information in the lending process; efficiency of competitive equilibrium in lending markets. Regulation and the conduct of monetary policy.
135.prereq_text: (ECN 101 or ECN 101Y or ECN 101V); (STA 013 or STA 013V or STA 013Y or STA 032).

138.title: Public Economics in International Perspective
138.description: Social problems and government responses in developed and developing countries; health, unemployment, informal insurance, poverty, corruption, and public service delivery; emphasis on quantitative and data analysis skills; applications to real world policy problems.
138.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have previously completed an upper division economics course in international public economics.
138.prereq_text: (ECN 100A or ECN 100AV or ECN 100 or ARE 100A); ECN 102.

140.title: Econometrics
140.description: Problems of observation, estimation and hypotheses testing in economics through the study of the theory and application of linear regression models. Critical evaluation of selected examples of empirical research and exercises in applied economics.
140.prereq_text: (ECN 100A or ECN 100AV or ECN 100AY or ARE 100A); (ECN 102 or STA 108); or consent of instructor.

142.title: Economics & Business Data Analytics
142.description: Introduction to economics and business data analytics. Statistical learning methods to analyze big data in economics and business data analysis. Statistical learning, linear regression, classification, resampling methods, and linear model selection and regularization.
142.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have previously completed an upper division economics course in economics and business data analytics.
142.prereq_text: (ECN 100A or ECN 100AV or ARE 100A); (ECN 102 B or better or ECN 140 B or better); (STA 013 or STA 013V or STA 013Y).

160A.title: International Microeconomics
160A.description: International trade theory: impact of trade on the domestic and world economies; public policy toward external trade.
160A.credit_limit_text: Only 2 units of credit allowed to students who have completed ECN 162.

160B.title: International Macroeconomics
160B.description: Macroeconomic theory of an open economy. Balance of payments adjustment mechanism, international monetary economics issues; international financial institutions and their policies.
160B.credit_limit_text: Only 2 units of credit allowed to students who have completed ECN 162.

171.title: Economy of East Asia
171.description: Intensive reading, discussion and research on selected topics from the economies of the countries of East Asia. Consult department for course scheduling.
171.prereq_text: (ECN 001A or ECN 001AY or ECN 001AV); (ECN 001B or ECN 001BV); or consent of instructor.

190.title: Topics in Economics
190.description: Selected topics in economic analysis and public policy. Variable content.

198.title: Directed Group Study
198.description: Directed group study. May be taught abroad.

199.title: Special Study for Advanced Undergraduates
199.description: Special study for advanced undergraduates. May be taught abroad.

200C.title: Microeconomic Theory
200C.description: Uncertainty and information economics. Individual decision making under uncertainty. Introduction to game theory, with emphasis on applications to markets with firms that are imperfect competitors or consumers that are imperfectly informed.

200E.title: Macroeconomic Theory
200E.description: Macrodynamic theory of income, employment, and prices.

215B.title: Open Macroeconomics of Development
215B.description: Models and policy approaches regarding trade, monetary and fiscal issues, capital flows and debt are discussed in the macroeconomic framework of an open developing country. Basic analytical focus is real exchange rate and its impact on sectoral allocation of resources.
215B.prereq_text: (ARE 200A or ECN 200A); (ARE 204 or ECN 204); (ECN 214 or ECN 215A); ECN 200D or ECN 205.

221B.title: Empirical Analysis in Industrial Organization
221B.description: Recent empirical work in industrial organization.  Topics include empirical analysis of cartels, product differentiation, innovation and technological change, and imperfect competition in international markets.

230B.title: Public Economics
230B.description: Effects of government policies on economic behavior; labor supply, program participation, investment, consumption and savings.

240A.title: Econometric Methods
240A.description: Least squares, instrumental variables, and maximum likelihood estimation and inference for single equation linear regression model; linear restrictions; heteroskedasticity; autocorrelation; lagged dependent variables.

240C.title: Time Series Econometrics
240C.description: Probability theory; estimation, inference and forecasting of time series models; trends and non-standard asymptotic theory; vector time series methods and cointegration; time series models for higher order moments and transition data; state-space modeling and the Kalman filter.

240F.title: Topics in Cross Section Econometrics
240F.description: Modern econometrics techniques for cross-section data. Expand on topics covered in ECN 240A, ECN 240B, ECN 240D. Content may differ year to year.

250A.title: Labor Economics
250A.description: Philosophy, theory and history of American and foreign labor movements; union structure, organization and collective bargaining under changing labor market conditions; current labor market issues.

260B.title: International Economics
260B.description: Balance of payments adjustment mechanisms; foreign exchange markets theories of balance of payments policy and international monetary mechanisms.

260E.title: Topics in International Trade
260E.description: Current literature in international trade theory.
